scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You glance at your phone in a dark room, and it unlocks instantly. How does it see you?

scenes.name: dots
scenes.text: On phones like the iPhone, a projector shoots over thirty thousand invisible infrared dots onto your face.

scenes.name: ir
scenes.text: An infrared camera reads how those dots land. They shift around your nose, cheeks and eyes. And infrared works in the dark.

scenes.name: map
scenes.text: From the dot pattern, it builds a depth map. A 3D shape of your face, not just a flat photo.

scenes.name: math
scenes.text: A neural network turns that shape into numbers, and compares them with the ones saved at setup, inside a secure chip.

scenes.name: spoof
scenes.text: Because it measures depth, a printed photo looks flat and fails. Apple says a random stranger matches about one in a million times.

scenes.name: basic
scenes.text: Many phones only use the front camera, a flat 2D match. That's easier to fool, and it needs some light.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Dots, depth, numbers, match. Your face, as a key. Follow for more on how things really work.
